You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

Based on the chest X-ray findings (Figure 4), which of the following statements best explains the diagnosis and distribution of calcifications in this patient, considering the expected radiographic patterns of pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis?

A) The calcifications are predominantly located in the upper left lobe, which is consistent with pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis due to the protective effect of paraseptal emphysema.

B) The calcifications are diffused throughout the lower lobes more extensively than in the upper left lobe, a pattern typical of pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis due to subpleural and peribronchovascular predominance.

C) The calcifications are predominantly linear and confined to the pleural surfaces, indicating a different condition than pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis.

D) The calcifications are absent in the lower lobes, which is unusual for pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis and suggests an alternative diagnosis.

E) There is a uniform distribution of calcifications across both lungs, which is atypical for pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis and points towards diffuse alveolar septal amyloidosis.

F) The calcifications are localized to the right lung, indicating a unilateral presentation inconsistent with pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis.
